name: What should I do first if my kitchen cabinets are always overflowing?

mainEntity.name: What should I do first if my kitchen cabinets are always overflowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start by listing what is difficult to store, where it is used, and what currently blocks access. A design-build consultation can then test whether the best fix is cabinet reconfiguration, new cabinetry, a pantry, or a broader kitchen remodel. Context: Storage improvements work best when they follow daily tasks rather than simply adding shelves. Group dishes near the sink or dishwasher, cookware near the range, and prep items near the main work surface. Key factors: cabinet depth; appliance clearances; wall and floor space; household routines. Practical guidance: Photograph crowded cabinets, measure openings, and note items that are used daily versus seasonally. Elite Remodeling & Design can incorporate these findings into layout development and 3D design before construction. This approach helps connect storage decisions with the rest of the kitchen plan.
acceptedAnswer.description: First, identify what is hard to store and where each item is used. Measure crowded cabinets, separate daily items from seasonal ones, and discuss whether pull-outs, new cabinets, a pantry, or a layout change best solves the problem.
